candidates: getBouncyCastleProvider() is documented to return the BouncyCastle (or BCFIPS) Provider, but this implementation returns the provider backing the default KeyStore type (often SUN). This breaks the interface contract and makes it harder for callers to reason about whether BC is available. Prefer returning the actual BC/BCFIPS provider by name (or null if not installed).

ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) calls are dead code (their results are discarded) and the method also creates multiple redundant encoder instances. This makes the intent harder to follow and does extra work.

Adding a new abstract method to a widely implemented interface is binary-incompatible for already-compiled CryptoProvider implementations (they will fail with AbstractMethodError at runtime). To preserve compatibility, make this a default method and let built-in providers override it as needed.

Provider selection can be non-deterministic when multiple CryptoProvider implementations return the same order(), because ServiceLoader iteration order is not guaranteed. Add a deterministic tie-breaker so the chosen provider is stable across environments.

logger.debugf(builder.toString()) treats the message as a format string; if any provider class name ever contained '%' it could misformat/throw. Also the current StringBuilder loop leaves a trailing ', '. Build the list with joining and pass it as a debugf parameter.
The exception message is grammatically awkward and doesn't include the actual size encountered, which makes debugging malformed signatures harder.

Throwing UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported yet.") is not very actionable when it bubbles up from CryptoIntegration. Include the provider/method name in the message so failures are diagnosable.
